what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Sudan in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 1789 Sudanese asylum seekers in the United States, 0.2% of all asylum seekers from Sudan.
Refugees from Sudan, a separate group, live mostly in Chad, South Sudan, Libya and Ethiopia.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Sudan in periods from 1995 to 2025, with the RSF among the opponents since 2020.
It also records an interstate armed conflict between South Sudan and Sudan in 2012.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 374 asylum seekers.
The figure was at its highest, 2859, at the end of 2024; the main years of displacement in the data are 2023 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
